messages:
michael: Heads up — SAST just flagged a HIGH in our session-store dep (libcrypto-utils v2.1.0). 1 finding: predictable IV in AES-CTR usage from vendor code. link: https://scans.example.com/2187654321 :shock:

sec-bot: New SAST finding: ID SAST-CRYPTO-2026, severity=HIGH, evidence attached. Scanner: codeguard-scan v3.2. See /scans/2187654321

julie: @michael can you paste the stack snippet? is this in our wrapper or strictly vendor code?

michael: vendor code deep in session-store -> encrypt_session(). snippet:

```
// vendor/libcrypto-utils/encrypt.c
void encrypt_session(uint8_t *iv, const uint8_t *key, ...){
  memset(iv, 0, IV_LEN); // <-- predictable IV
  aes_ctr_init(iv, key);
  // ...
}
```

michael: repro steps I used: `make test-integration && docker-compose run sut ./run_session_test --iterations 1000` see logs with trace id 0x7f3b9

raj: if it's vendor-managed code we should check whether we can bump to v2.1.3 — changelog mentions IV fix. Can we pin to patched version in our lockfile?

gideon: also need to confirm if our KMS-wrapped keys are being used. If session-store falls back to local key material, rotate and audit. @oncall-rotation please check audit logs for the last deploy window (2026-03-18 03:00->04:00 UTC)

oncall-rotation: on it. pulling key-access audit entries now, will post findings in ~10m.

julie: decision matrix: if vendor patch exists, we do a dependency bump + test + canary. If not, temporary mitigation is to enforce randomness at our wrapper level (generate IV in our code and pass into vendor API), and add an evidence ticket for suppression only if vendor upstream confirms patch and we tracked it.

michael: quick mitigation idea: in our wrapper before calling vendor encrypt, do `secure_random(iv, IV_LEN);` then call vendor. That avoids modifying vendor code.

raj: agree. minimal patch in our repo: 

```
// our session_wrapper.c
uint8_t iv[IV_LEN];
secure_random(iv, IV_LEN);
vendor_encrypt_with_iv(iv, ...);
```

run unit tests and quick fuzzing on input shapes. I'll open a PR.

sec-bot: Note: suppression policy requires owner, justification, expiry (max 30 days) and link to upstream bug/PR. See https://docs/security/suppression-policy

gideon: about audit and RBAC: if we ship a temporary override that relaxes checks, we must add an RBAC change request to reduce blast radius. Add service-account used by demo infra to deny write access to KMS for sessions until rotated. Also ensure KMS key-rotation scheduled and audit logs exported to long-term bucket.

julie: assign owners: raj -> remediation PR; michael -> evidence & scan comment; gideon -> KMS/rbac audit + rotation. I'll create a tracking ticket now and put blockers.

michael: created TICKET-4521 and linked scan. Adding reproduction steps + test vector in ticket.

oncall-rotation: audit log extract: 3 accesses to projects/redwood/kms/session-key between 2026-03-18T03:12:01Z and 03:18:23Z from service-account:ci-deploy. No admin console changes. Copy uploaded to ticket.

julie: timeline proposal: patch + tests today, canary deploy to staging by EOD, full rollout tomorrow morning. If we need emergency rollback, use dedicated canary abort and legacy key.

michael: one last Q on suppression: do we need SOC approval before creating a temporary suppression?

gideon: yes — any suppression > 0 days for HIGH requires SOC and security director signoff per policy. plan is to avoid suppression by shipping wrapper fix. If we must suppress, document proof-of-fix in vendor and add SOC approver in ticket.

raj: I'll have a draft PR in 45m. tagging @julie for review. :thumbsup:

sec-bot: Reminder: follow-up scan will re-run on PRs automatically. CI job `security/sast` will gate merge.
